title: API endpoint
summary: Auth on every verb, object and function authorization, mass assignment, content-type swaps, and URL-fetching fields. Two accounts minimum.

groups.title: Authorization
groups.summary: Swap the object, the verb, and the caller. That is most of API testing.

checks.title: Object-level authorization (BOLA)
checks.why: The handler trusts the object id in the path or body more than the caller.
checks.validate: Account B reads or changes account A's object. Confirm against a fresh authoritative read.

variants.name: Swap the path id
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: 1002 belongs to account B. Repeat as PUT/PATCH/DELETE on the same id.
variants.why: Reading another tenant's object via its path id with your token is the canonical BOLA.

variants.name: Swap in the JSON body
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/orders/1001 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1002,"status":"cancelled"}
variants.expect: Body id must not retarget the update. Also try user_id, account_id, tenant_id, org_id.
variants.why: The object id in the body may bind a different object than the route path, bypassing the check.

variants.name: Numeric walk
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1000 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: 1000, 1001, 1002. A 200 for another tenant is the finding. Stop after a few hits.
variants.why: Sequential ids let one token sweep the object space.

variants.name: Nested and bulk
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders/export HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":[1001,1002,1003]}
variants.expect: Each member needs its own decision. Also /orders/1001/items/55 and /graphql node(id:).
variants.why: Nested or batch endpoints can fetch objects the top-level endpoint authorizes individually.

checks.title: Function-level authorization (BFLA)
checks.why: Admin routes exist in the spec, the JS bundle, or an older version, and a member token can call them.
checks.validate: A privileged function executes for a caller the matrix denies.

variants.name: Member token on an admin route
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: 403/404, not a user list. Repeat /internal/, /debug/, /actuator/, /manage/.
variants.why: A low-privilege token invoking an admin function is function-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Verb swap
variants.payload:
DELETE /api/v1/users/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: GET may be allowed and DELETE not. Also PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS.
variants.why: The same route may authorize GET but not DELETE; swapping the verb bypasses the check.

variants.name: Version and alias
variants.payload:
GET /api/v0/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: Older versions, /api/users vs /api/user, trailing slashes, and case variants.
variants.why: An older API version or alias route may not inherit the current authorization.

checks.title: Mass assignment / extra properties
checks.why: The binder accepts role, price, owner, or verified flags the UI never sends.
checks.validate: An unlisted property is stored and later returned or enforced.

variants.name: Hidden privilege fields
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"role":"admin","isAdmin":true,"verified":true,"price":0}
variants.expect: Read the object back. role/isAdmin/verified/price/balance/tenant_id must be unchanged.
variants.why: Sending undeclared properties maps them to model attributes the API never intended to expose.

variants.name: JSON nested wrapper
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"user":{"role":"admin"},"role":"admin"}
variants.expect: Some binders take the nested object, some the top-level key. Try both.
variants.why: Nested wrappers can smuggle privilege fields past a flat allowlist.

groups.title: Protocol and schema
groups.summary: Missing auth, content-type confusion, and method override.

checks.title: Missing or alternate authentication
checks.why: The same route accepts no token, an expired token, or a token in a different place.
checks.validate: A protected resource returns data without a current credential.

variants.name: Drop the Authorization header
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: 401, not 200 with data. Repeat on every interesting route, not only /me.
variants.why: A 200 with the token removed means the resource is not actually gated.

variants.name: Token in the query string
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders?access_token=<token> HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If it works, the token is now in logs and Referer. Prefer that it does not work.
variants.why: A bearer accepted from the query string leaks into logs, caches, and Referer.

variants.name: Expired and wrong-audience JWT
variants.payload: Replay a captured token after logout, after expiry, and against a sibling API on the same issuer.
variants.expect: Must fail. See the JWT playbook checks in the methodology for alg=none and kid tricks.
variants.why: Accepted expired or wrong-audience tokens mean expiry and audience are not enforced.

checks.title: Content-Type and verb override
checks.why: A JSON-only handler that also parses form or text/plain skips CSRF and schema checks.
checks.validate: The same body is accepted under a different type or verb and changes state.

variants.name: JSON as form
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

id=1002&status=cancelled
variants.expect: Rejected, or parsed and authorized the same way as JSON. A silent parse is the interesting case.
variants.why: Frameworks may parse the same body differently by Content-Type, altering which parameters are bound.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain (CSRF-simple)
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example

{"status":"cancelled"}
variants.expect: Must not change state. This is the classic simple-request CSRF shape.
variants.why: A text/plain JSON POST skips a preflight and can be CSRF'd unless a token is required.

variants.name: X-HTTP-Method-Override
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders/1001 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE
Content-Length: 0
variants.expect: Override must not reach a handler the real DELETE would refuse. Also try _method=DELETE.
variants.why: A header override changes the effective verb the route authorizes.

checks.title: Server-side URL parameters
checks.why: webhook, import, avatar, and preview fields make the server fetch a URL you choose.
checks.validate: A callback on a host you control, or an internal destination, is fetched. Use Collaborator / a canary, never cloud metadata on a shared environment without approval.

variants.name: Collaborator HTTPS
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/hooks HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"url":"https://unique.oast.example/wapt"}
variants.expect: An outbound HTTP hit on your listener. Repeat for image, callback, feed, avatar, import_url, pdf, sitemap.
variants.why: A controlled HTTPS callback confirms the server makes the outbound request.

variants.name: Redirect follow
variants.payload: Point url at https://unique.oast.example/302 which 302s to http://127.0.0.1/.
variants.expect: The server must not follow to loopback. Do not hit cloud metadata unless the owner approved an isolated test.
variants.why: A redirect-following fetcher can be steered to an internal address the first request was denied.

variants.name: Scheme and userinfo
variants.payload:
file:///etc/passwd
gopher://127.0.0.1:6379/_
http://127.0.0.1#@unique.oast.example/
http://unique.oast.example@127.0.0.1/
variants.expect: Schemes outside http/https should be refused. Parser differentials on userinfo are common.
variants.why: Scheme/userinfo tricks in the URL are parsed differently by the SSRF guard and the actual client.

groups.title: GraphQL extras
groups.summary: Only when a GraphQL transport is in scope.

checks.title: Introspection and suggestions
checks.why: Production introspection or field suggestions disclose the schema the client never ships.
checks.validate: __schema or a typo suggestion returns fields the public contract does not list.

variants.name: Classic introspection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{__schema{types{name fields{name}}}}"}
variants.expect: Disabled in production, or limited to an allowlisted consumer. A full dump is a lead plus any hidden mutations.
variants.why: Introspection reveals the schema; disabling it is the expected production posture.

variants.name: Field suggestion
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{user{emial}}"}
variants.expect: "Did you mean email?" confirms names even when introspection is off.
variants.why: GraphQL suggestions disclose field names even when introspection is blocked.

checks.title: GraphQL object and field authorization
checks.why: node(id:), aliases, and nested edges skip the authorization the REST path has.
checks.validate: A field or node belonging to another account is returned.

variants.name: node(id:) swap
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{node(id:\"T3JkZXI6MTAwMg==\"){... on Order{id total}}}"}
variants.expect: Order 1002 is B's. Decode and recode other type prefixes too.
variants.why: Reading another object by global id is object-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Hidden field selection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{me{id email role passwordHash ssn}}"}
variants.expect: role, hashes, and internal fields must be absent or unauthorized — not merely omitted by the default client query.
variants.why: Fields with per-field authorization can leak data via a query that selects them directly.

checks.title: Object authorization on API mutations
checks.why: Reads get checked, writes get shipped — mutations are where object-level authorization is most often missing.
checks.validate: POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on another account or tenant object is refused with 403/404 and no side effects.

variants.name: Swap the body id
variants.payload: PATCH /api/objects with {"id": 1002, "name": "x"} as account A — 1002 belongs to test account B.
variants.expect: 403/404; B object unchanged (verify via B).
variants.why: Body-borne ids skip route guards that only inspect paths.

variants.name: Create referencing foreign parent
variants.payload: POST /api/tasks with {"project_id": <B-project>} as A.
variants.expect: Refused — creating under a foreign parent is an authorization decision.
variants.why: Write-side nesting is the classic gap.

variants.name: Delete via alias route
variants.payload: Repeat the foreign-object mutation on every alias shape found: /v2/objects, POST /objects/1002/archive, PATCH with tombstone flags.
variants.expect: Same refusal on all shapes — enforcement is object-level, not route-level.
variants.why: Aliases multiply forgotten checks.

checks.title: Nested and related API resources authorized
checks.why: Relations (sub-resources, includes, links) re-expose objects the primary endpoint correctly guards.
checks.validate: Every traversal path to a related object (nested route, include=, expand, _embed, link header) enforces the same authorization.

variants.name: Include/embed traversal
variants.payload: GET /api/orders/1001?include=customer with a B-customer relation on an A-order.
variants.expect: Related objects are filtered by caller permission — no cross-account includes.
variants.why: Includes serialize relations without re-authorizing them.

variants.name: Reverse relation hop
variants.payload: GET /api/customers/<B-id>/orders (list through the foreign parent).
variants.expect: 403/404 — the parent gate holds in both traversal directions.
variants.why: Inverse relations are forgotten guards.

variants.name: Link-header follow
variants.payload: Follow every relation URL the API itself returns for an A object (Link headers, _links, HAL).
variants.expect: Only caller-authorized relations resolve; returned links never leak foreign ids unguarded.
variants.why: Server-provided links are an honest map of weak spots.

checks.title: Batch members authorized independently
checks.why: One authorization decision per batch request launders every foreign member inside it.
checks.validate: Each member of an array/batch request is authorized and validated individually, with per-member error reporting.

variants.name: Mixed array
variants.payload: PUT /api/objects/batch with items=[{A-own ok}, {B-foreign}] as A.
variants.expect: Per-member refusal of B without partial application; response names the failing member only.
variants.why: The minimal honest batch probe.

variants.name: Duplicate member confusion
variants.payload: Same object id twice in one batch with different operations (update + delete).
variants.expect: Deterministic ordering per documented semantics; no double-apply or check-bypass via repetition.
variants.why: Arrays are ordered; authorization must not be.

variants.name: Nested batch shapes
variants.payload: Repeat via every batch transport: JSON arrays, NDJSON, patch+JSON arrays, bulk keys in query.
variants.expect: Same enforcement across transports.
variants.why: One guarded transport and one open twin.

checks.title: Mobile API access constrained across accounts and tenants
checks.why: Mobile clients often get a wider, older API surface with looser checks than the web client.
checks.validate: The mobile API surface enforces the same object and tenant authorization as the web API, with no legacy widenings.

variants.name: Cross-client replay
variants.payload: Capture the mobile app requests (proxy the device/emulator); replay your best web-side authorization probes against the mobile routes.
variants.expect: Same refusals — client type does not widen authority.
variants.why: The same identity, two doors, one policy.

variants.name: Legacy route hunt
variants.payload: Diff mobile routes vs web routes; probe mobile-only routes with cross-account ids.
variants.expect: Mobile-only routes enforce current authorization; legacy widenings reported.
variants.why: Mobile keeps old routes alive for years.

variants.name: Device-bound claims
variants.payload: If device ids/headers bind sessions, replay a captured request with a different device header from your own second device.
variants.expect: Device changes re-authenticate or re-validate per policy; no silent adoption.
variants.why: Device binding must be a control, not a decoration.

checks.title: Sensitive properties filtered from API responses
checks.why: API serializers dump full models — cost price, tokens, internal flags, PII ride along in JSON nobody reviews.
checks.validate: Responses contain only fields the caller may read; sensitive fields are absent (not null) for lesser roles.

variants.name: Two-role field diff
variants.payload: Fetch the same object type as two roles you hold; diff response keys.
variants.expect: Sensitive keys absent for the lesser role — a structural diff, not a value read.
variants.why: Object-level pass with field-level fail.

variants.name: Sparse fieldsets probe
variants.payload: Explicitly request sensitive fields via field selectors: ?fields=cost_price,internal_note / GraphQL-style projections.
variants.expect: Selectors cannot summon unauthorized fields.
variants.why: Field selection is user input, not permission.

variants.name: Error-shape leakage
variants.payload: Trigger validation errors after the sensitive field; compare error responses for presence hints.
variants.expect: Errors do not confirm or echo unauthorized field values.
variants.why: Error serializers forget filters too.

checks.title: Unauthorized property updates rejected
checks.why: Accept-everything PATCH handlers let callers edit balance, status, tier, owner — fields they can see but must not write.
checks.validate: Writable fields are explicitly allowlisted per role; protected fields reject or ignore with no partial application.

variants.name: Protected-field PATCH
variants.payload: PATCH /api/orders/1001 with {"status":"approved","total":0} as a standard user.
variants.expect: Protected fields rejected/ignored; the rest of the update follows documented policy.
variants.why: One payload tests both field classes.

variants.name: Unknown-field smuggling
variants.payload: Include undocumented keys (is_admin, internal_flag, owner_id, tenant_id) in updates.
variants.expect: Unknown keys rejected or ignored — never interpreted.
variants.why: Framework mass-binding turns typos into privileges.

variants.name: Type-confusion writes
variants.payload: Send the protected field with unexpected types (object, array, string-number) seeking a validator bypass.
variants.expect: Type juggling changes nothing; validation is type-strict per field.
variants.why: Coercion quirks open the same door as missing checks.

checks.title: Field authorization on sparse, expanded, alternate representations
checks.why: The detail endpoint filters fields; exports, embeds, expansions, CSV, and error previews quietly re-serialize everything.
checks.validate: Every representation (expand, include, export, alternate format, error echo) applies the same field rules.

variants.name: Expand/CSV sweep
variants.payload: Request the object with ?expand=*, csv export, and the mobile shape; repeat the two-role field diff on each.
variants.expect: Identical field visibility across representations.
variants.why: Serializers multiply; policies must keep up.

variants.name: Sparse-request round trip
variants.payload: Request with sparse fieldsets, then PUT the returned representation back with a protected field edited.
variants.expect: Round-trips do not grant write permission on read-visible fields.
variants.why: Readable JSON is not a writable contract.

variants.name: Pagination metadata leak
variants.payload: Inspect page metadata, facet counts, and aggregate fields for cross-account totals.
variants.expect: Aggregates respect the same authorization as rows.
variants.why: Sums and counts leak without a single row.

checks.title: Overfetch bounded to the operation contract
checks.why: Endpoints that return everything the caller could ask for leak data and enable scraping beyond the UI contract.
checks.validate: Responses return contracted fields/objects only; undocumented expansion (fields=*, deep includes) is refused.

variants.name: Wildcard expansion
variants.payload: GET /api/objects?fields=*, include=*, expand=3+ levels.
variants.expect: Wildcards and deep expansions refused or capped; contract enforced server-side.
variants.why: Ask for everything, see what you get.

variants.name: Cross-object join
variants.payload: Filter one resource by fields of another (?user.email=...) where the UI never offers it.
variants.expect: Only documented filter dimensions accepted.
variants.why: Accidental query APIs over relations.

variants.name: Scraper-shaped request
variants.payload: One request asking for maximum page size, all fields, all includes at once.
variants.expect: Bounded response per operation contract; document the ceiling for the report.
variants.why: One request, one contract.

groups.title: API keys, tokens, and protocol parity

checks.title: API keys scoped, revocable, and server-side
checks.why: Broad, immortal, client-shipped API keys are permanent backdoors; scope and revocability decide blast radius.
checks.validate: Keys are least-scoped, revocable instantly, rotated, and never shipped in clients; server-side secrets never reach bundles.

variants.name: Scope fence
variants.payload: With two of your own keys (narrow + broad), use the narrow one beyond its scope.
variants.expect: Out-of-scope calls fail — scope enforced at execution, not display.
variants.why: The key says what it may do; the server must agree.

variants.name: Revoke and replay
variants.payload: Revoke a key; immediately replay a known-good request.
variants.expect: Dead instantly (within documented window); measure it.
variants.why: Revocation is the kill switch.

variants.name: Client-bundle hunt
variants.payload: Grep shipped web/mobile bundles for key patterns (AKIA-, sk_, api_key, long base64 near config).
variants.expect: No live secrets in distributed code; found keys verified harmlessly then reported.
variants.why: A key in a bundle is public by definition.

checks.title: API tokens bound to audience and type
checks.why: A token minted for service A validating at service B collapses API boundaries — token audience is the boundary.
checks.validate: Each API validates aud and token type (access vs ID vs refresh) for itself; wrong-audience tokens are rejected.

variants.name: Cross-service token
variants.payload: Use the token obtained for API A directly against API B (both first-party).
variants.expect: B rejects with an audience error — not a downstream permission error.
variants.why: Reject at the door, not deep inside.

variants.name: Token-type confusion
variants.payload: Send the ID token and (if separate) the refresh token as an access token on API calls.
variants.expect: Rejected — each endpoint accepts exactly one token type.
variants.why: OIDC confusion in API clothing.

variants.name: Stale-version token
variants.payload: Use a v1-issued token (if versions coexist) on v2 endpoints.
variants.expect: Same audience rules across versions; version drift never widens acceptance.
variants.why: Versions must not become audiences.

checks.title: Equivalent authentication across versions and protocols
checks.why: When v2 enforces MFA/signed requests and v1 or an alternate protocol does not, attackers use the weaker door.
checks.validate: Authentication strength (MFA, signing, device checks) is equivalent across versions, protocols, and transports.

variants.name: Version downgrade
variants.payload: Replay authenticated calls through every version marker (path /v1, Accept header, ?version=).
variants.expect: Same authentication enforced on all versions; weaker elders reported.
variants.why: Enumerate versions before trusting parity.

variants.name: Protocol alternates
variants.payload: Repeat via alternate transports the API offers: SOAP wrapper, gRPC endpoint, GraphQL — same operation, same auth.
variants.expect: Equivalent enforcement across protocols.
variants.why: Each protocol has its own middleware history.

variants.name: MFA bypass route
variants.payload: Where the web flow requires MFA, find API paths (password grant, legacy login, direct session create) that do not.
variants.expect: All authentication paths enforce the same assurance level.
variants.why: The bypass is a route, not a flaw in the main door.

checks.title: Page size and result windows bounded
checks.why: Unbounded pagination is a full-database export button and a self-DoS lever in one parameter.
checks.validate: Page size, offset/cursor windows, and expansion depth are capped server-side with documented maxima.

variants.name: Size inflation
variants.payload: GET /api/objects?limit=999999 (and page_size, count, per_page variants).
variants.expect: Capped at the documented maximum — not echoed, not honored.
variants.why: Parameter name roulette with one expected answer.

variants.name: Deep offset
variants.payload: Walk offset/page to extreme values (page=99999).
variants.expect: Windowed or refused; cost bounded — no deep-offset scans.
variants.why: Deep pagination is a scan primitive.

variants.name: Expansion depth
variants.payload: include=a.b.c.d chains to the maximum the schema allows and beyond.
variants.expect: Depth capped; beyond-cap refused with a clear error.
variants.why: Every include level multiplies the query.

checks.title: Request body, array, and batch sizes bounded
checks.why: Giant bodies and huge arrays parse before authorization — resource exhaustion before the first check.
checks.validate: Body size, array lengths, and batch counts are limited before processing, with clear errors at the limit.

variants.name: Array inflation
variants.payload: POST a batch with 10k members (ids of your own objects).
variants.expect: Refused above the documented batch cap with a clear error; no partial processing.
variants.why: Your own objects make the probe honest.

variants.name: Deep-nesting payload
variants.payload: Send JSON nested to 100+ levels in a normal field.
variants.expect: Rejected by depth limits before parsing completes; parser limits configured.
variants.why: Parsers die before validators run.

variants.name: Oversized field
variants.payload: One field with a multi-MB string in an update you legitimately own.
variants.expect: Field length limits enforced per documented maximums.
variants.why: Size limits are per field, not just per request.

checks.title: Expensive filters, sorts, and joins bounded
checks.why: Sorts on unindexed fields and wildcard searches turn one cheap endpoint into a database scanner.
checks.validate: Filter/sort parameters are allowlisted; expensive operations are capped, timed out, or rate-limited.

variants.name: Sort-field roulette
variants.payload: sort= on every field of the response, including computed and relation fields.
variants.expect: Only indexed/allowlisted sorts accepted; others 400.
variants.why: Sort injection is a performance exploit.

variants.name: Wildcard search
variants.payload: Search for %, *, single chars, and leading wildcards where search exists.
variants.expect: Leading-wildcard/expensive patterns refused or capped; response times stable.
variants.why: Watch latency, not just status.

variants.name: Filter stacking
variants.payload: Stack many AND/OR filters and ranges in one request.
variants.expect: Complexity capped; combinatorial requests rejected.
variants.why: Query builders assemble DoS politely.

checks.title: Paid and async side effects limited
checks.why: APIs that send mail, SMS, invoke paid AI, or start jobs burn real money and reputation when called in a loop.
checks.validate: Metered side effects are quota-limited, rate-limited, and require appropriate authorization per trigger.

variants.name: Quota probe
variants.payload: Trigger the metered action toward its documented quota (small counts only, on your own account).
variants.expect: Quota enforced with a clear error at the cap; no silent metering gaps.
variants.why: Spend as little as the evidence needs.

variants.name: Authorization on the trigger
variants.payload: Trigger side-effecting endpoints for objects/scopes you cannot access.
variants.expect: Refused — side effects inherit object authorization.
variants.why: Cost follows permission.

variants.name: Async flooding
variants.payload: Enqueue the maximum documented parallel jobs for your account.
variants.expect: Concurrent-job cap enforced per account; queue backpressure visible.
variants.why: Background work is still abuse surface.

checks.title: Concurrent and distributed abuse controls
checks.why: Per-connection limits fall to a few parallel clients; abuse controls must count identity, not sockets.
checks.validate: Limits key on account/identity across connections and IPs, with graduated responses and safe-by-default errors.

variants.name: Parallel identity
variants.payload: Fire a small parallel burst (3-5 concurrent) of identical requests from one identity across two source IPs if available.
variants.expect: Identity-level throttling engages regardless of connection count.
variants.why: Two IPs, one account, one counter.

variants.name: Graduated response
variants.payload: Observe response behavior across the throttle boundary (Retry-After, 429 shape).
variants.expect: 429 with Retry-After; no stack traces, no lockout-without-recovery.
variants.why: Errors are part of the control design.

variants.name: Expensive-op combination
variants.payload: Combine the throttled op with the most expensive filter from the previous checks in one call.
variants.expect: The tighter of the two limits wins; no bypass via combined shape.
variants.why: Limits compose or they fail.

checks.title: High-value business flows protected from automation
checks.why: Signup, referral, coupon, voting, and messaging flows monetized by bots at API speed are business-logic abuse.
checks.validate: High-value flows have automation controls (proof-of-work, captchas, velocity rules) proportionate to value.

variants.name: Velocity profile
variants.payload: Exercise one protected flow (signup on a disposable domain, or referral with your two accounts) at API speed for a handful of iterations.
variants.expect: Velocity rules engage per documented policy — slowdowns, challenges, or caps.
variants.why: Measure the control, do not defeat it.

variants.name: Missing-control diff
variants.payload: Compare web UI protections (captcha, confirmation) vs the raw API path for the same flow.
variants.expect: API paths carry equivalent friction — no captcha-free twin.
variants.why: The UI is polite; the API must be too.

variants.name: Cross-flow composition
variants.payload: Chain two benign flows (signup + referral + redemption) at API speed with your own accounts.
variants.expect: Composition bounded; each stage carries its own controls.
variants.why: Abuse is often a pipeline, not a call.

checks.title: Function policy across methods and aliases
checks.why: One function, many spellings: method overrides, trailing slashes, and case variants skip route-level decisions.
checks.validate: Authorization and policy bind to the function, applied across every method, path spelling, and alias route.

variants.name: Method override headers
variants.payload: POST /api/objects/1002/delete with X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE (and _method=DELETE body/query).
variants.expect: Override headers do not bypass the policy attached to the real method.
variants.why: Proxies and frameworks honor overrides — policies must too.

variants.name: Path spelling roulette
variants.payload: Retry guarded calls as /api/objects/1002/, /api/Objects/1002, /api//objects/1002, /api/v1.5/objects/1002.
variants.expect: All spellings hit the same guard; normalization is uniform.
variants.why: Routers normalize; authorization may not follow.

variants.name: Trailing-verb aliases
variants.payload: Probe action-style aliases (POST /objects/1002/approve vs PATCH status=approved).
variants.expect: Aliases enforce the same authorization as the canonical shape.
variants.why: Every alias is a separate policy decision point.

checks.title: API role and membership management constrained
checks.why: Admin/role/invite functions behind API calls are privilege minting — the most valuable endpoints in the product.
checks.validate: Role, membership, and permission management functions require layered authorization and audit every call.

variants.name: Self-service elevation
variants.payload: As a standard account, call role-assign/invite endpoints granting yourself an admin role.
variants.expect: Refused and logged — layered checks, not one role string.
variants.why: The privilege-minting probe on your own account.

variants.name: Scope-bounded admin
variants.payload: As tenant-1 admin, call the same functions for tenant-2 principals.
variants.expect: Cross-scope refused; admin of one is not admin of all.
variants.why: Scoped admins are the multi-tenant rule.

variants.name: Audit trail check
variants.payload: After owner-assisted legitimate role changes, inspect the audit view for the events.
variants.expect: Every role/membership change is recorded with actor, target, and before/after.
variants.why: Minting without a trail is unaccountable.

checks.title: Undocumented API functions denied by default
checks.why: Routes missing from the policy inventory inherit framework defaults — usually authenticated-and-allowed.
checks.validate: Undocumented/newly deployed functions deny by default until a policy explicitly allows them.

variants.name: Dark-route probe
variants.payload: Probe routes seen in JS bundles but not in the UI or docs (feature-flagged endpoints) as a standard user.
variants.expect: Denied without explicit policy; accessible dark routes reported.
variants.why: Bundles leak the roadmap; policy should already cover it.

variants.name: Inventory diff
variants.payload: Diff OpenAPI/docs against observed proxy-history routes; sample-call the undocumented set harmlessly.
variants.expect: Undocumented functions denied or documented-as-intended.
variants.why: The dark API is bigger than the bright one.

variants.name: Guessable next-versions
variants.payload: Probe /v(N+1)/ and common upcoming resource names for reachability.
variants.expect: Unreleased surfaces unreachable or fully guarded.
variants.why: Predictable names meet unpredicable policy.

checks.title: Workflow sequence and state prerequisites enforced
checks.why: Skipping steps via API (checkout without payment, publish without review) breaks business invariants cheaply.
checks.validate: Each step validates the object state and prerequisites the workflow defines — order is authorization.

variants.name: Skip-ahead
variants.payload: Fire a late-state operation (complete, publish, payout) directly on a fresh object.
variants.expect: Refused — sequence enforced server-side.
variants.why: Steps the UI enforces are steps the API must too.

variants.name: Out-of-order replay
variants.payload: Execute steps in reverse where possible (refund before capture equivalents in harmless flows).
variants.expect: Rejected; state machine validated per transition.
variants.why: Reverse order finds missing guards.

variants.name: Prerequisite-field forgery
variants.payload: Submit a step with prerequisite fields claiming completion (paid=true, approved=true) before the real prerequisite ran.
variants.expect: Server verifies prerequisites from authoritative state, not payload claims.
variants.why: Client-attested prerequisites are not prerequisites.

checks.title: Idempotency and one-time semantics on transactions
checks.why: Networks retry; without idempotency keys every retry duplicates orders, charges, and invitations.
checks.validate: Mutating operations honor idempotency keys (or are naturally idempotent); one-time tokens are single-use atomically.

variants.name: Idempotency-key replay
variants.payload: Send the same Idempotency-Key on two identical creates; then two different payloads under one key.
variants.expect: Same key+payload returns the original result; different payload under the same key is an error.
variants.why: The documented contract, tested literally.

variants.name: One-time token reuse
variants.payload: Redeem a one-time token (invitation, coupon, OTP-confirmed action) twice in quick succession.
variants.expect: Second use fails; single-use enforced atomically.
variants.why: One-time means one under race too.

variants.name: Retry-storm shape
variants.payload: Fire a 3-request retry burst of a non-idempotent create (network-retry shape).
variants.expect: At most one effect; duplicates prevented or safely reconciled.
variants.why: Retries are the honest attack.

checks.title: Server-side fetch redirects and resolved addresses revalidated
checks.why: A URL parameter the server fetches is SSRF; redirects that skip revalidation carry the fetch anywhere internal.
checks.validate: Fetched URLs are allowlisted; redirects are revalidated per-hop (scheme, host, address); private ranges blocked.

variants.name: Redirect to internal
variants.payload: Point a fetch-preview/import URL at your Collaborator that 302s to http://169.254.169.254/ and internal names.
variants.expect: No internal fetch occurs; every hop revalidated; interaction logged.
variants.why: Redirect-following is where URL filters die.

variants.name: Scheme and address tricks
variants.payload: URLs with redirects to gopher://, redirects to decimal/hex IP encodings of private ranges.
variants.expect: Scheme pinned to http(s); address-family checks decode encodings before deciding.
variants.why: Encodings bypass naive string filters.

variants.name: DNS-rebinding shape
variants.payload: A hostname you control resolving to a private IP on second lookup (interact safely, document only).
variants.expect: Resolution re-checked per fetch or egress-bound; rebinding documented as mitigated or present.
variants.why: Name-based allowlists without pinning are bypassable.

checks.title: Unsupported methods and media types rejected
checks.why: TRACE, unexpected verbs, and exotic content-types walk into parsers and handlers with different rules.
checks.validate: Only documented methods and media types are accepted; everything else fails closed before processing.

variants.name: Verb roulette
variants.payload: OPTIONS, TRACE, CONNECT, PATCH-on-read-only, and arbitrary X-CUSTOM verbs on a normal resource.
variants.expect: 405 with Allow; TRACE never echoes; unknown verbs do not route.
variants.why: The verb table is policy.

variants.name: Content-type confusion
variants.payload: POST with text/plain, application/xml, x-www-form-encoded carrying JSON bodies to JSON endpoints (and vice versa).
variants.expect: Only accepted media types parsed; confusion rejected — no CSRF-relevant parsing surprises.
variants.why: Parsing differences are deserialization and CSRF surface.

variants.name: Accept-shape leaks
variants.payload: Request Accept: text/html, application/xml on API endpoints.
variants.expect: No HTML error pages with stack traces; acceptable representations only.
variants.why: Error negotiators forget filters.

checks.title: Debug modes, stack traces, and internals removed
checks.why: Stack traces and debug payloads hand over versions, paths, keys, and queries in one response.
checks.validate: Production errors are shape-stable without stack traces, query text, internal ids, or debug flags.

variants.name: Error-shape audit
variants.payload: Trigger validation, auth, and 500-class errors (harmlessly); inspect bodies and headers.
variants.expect: Correlation id only — no stacks, driver errors, SQL fragments, or file paths.
variants.why: Every error handler is a disclosure decision.

variants.name: Debug-flag roulette
variants.payload: Append ?debug=1, X-Debug: true, and common staging headers to normal requests.
variants.expect: Debug output absent in production regardless of flags.
variants.why: Flags that worked in staging ship to prod.

variants.name: Verbose-header check
variants.payload: Inspect response headers for X-Powered-By, Server versions, internal hostnames, request ids that leak topology.
variants.expect: Minimal header set; version/internal detail absent.
variants.why: Headers are the free reconnaissance channel.

checks.title: CORS by exact origin with credential need
checks.why: Reflective or wildcard CORS with credentials turns any origin into an authenticated client.
checks.validate: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is an exact allowlisted origin; credentials only where required; no wildcard+credentials.

variants.name: Origin reflection
variants.payload: Send Origin: https://evil.example on a credentialed endpoint; read ACAO/ACAC headers.
variants.expect: No reflection — allowlisted exact origins only; evil origin gets no ACAO or a null allow.
variants.why: The one-request CORS verdict.

variants.name: Subdomain and lookalike
variants.payload: Origin values like https://www.example.com.evil.example and https://evilwww combos.
variants.expect: Rejected — suffix/prefix matching is not origin matching.
variants.why: String-contains CORS is a browser-level bypass.

variants.name: Preflight honesty
variants.payload: Trigger preflights with custom headers; inspect Access-Control-Allow-Headers/Methods.
variants.expect: Only documented headers/methods allowed; no * with credentials.
variants.why: Preflight answers describe the real policy.

checks.title: Schemas, consoles, and management endpoints protected
checks.why: Swagger UIs, GraphQL consoles, metrics, and management ports reveal the whole map — often unauthenticated.
checks.validate: Schema/console/metrics/management surfaces are authenticated, authorization-gated, and stripped from production where unused.

variants.name: Map fetch
variants.payload: GET /swagger, /openapi.json, /graphql (IDE), /metrics, /actuator, /health/detail, /api-docs unauthenticated.
variants.expect: Denied or minimized per surface; anything exposed documented as intended.
variants.why: One GET per name, then judgment.

variants.name: Management actions
variants.payload: Where actuator/management endpoints exist, attempt read-only listings first (env, beans, mappings) — never state-changing.
variants.expect: Read-only listings denied in production; no write access at all.
variants.why: Look, do not touch.

variants.name: Console via API
variants.payload: Where a GraphQL/REST console exists in production, check it requires an authenticated, authorized session.
variants.expect: Console gated like the API itself — it is the API.
variants.why: Consoles are the API wearing a UI.

checks.title: Inventory of API hosts, paths, and owners
checks.why: You cannot authorize, deprecate, or retire what nobody has listed — the inventory is every later check's base map.
checks.validate: A maintained inventory of API hosts, base paths, protocols, versions, and owning teams.

variants.name: Discovery triangulation
variants.payload: Build the list from documentation, proxy history, JS bundle route extraction, and well-known files; merge into one inventory.
variants.expect: Inventory cross-checked with the owner; unknowns become scope questions, not assumptions.
variants.why: Four sources beat one.

variants.name: Host and path sweep
variants.payload: Check api., app., mobile., graphql., admin. subdomains plus /api, /v1..v3, /graphql, /rpc base paths in scope.
variants.expect: Every discovered host mapped to an owner and a retirement policy.
variants.why: Naming conventions predict deployment.

variants.name: Owner confirmation
variants.payload: Review the inventory with the owner; mark in-scope, out-of-scope, and unknown-owner.
variants.expect: Signed-off inventory — the engagement scope statement for API work.
variants.why: Scope honesty starts here.

checks.title: Deprecated API versions identified and retired
checks.why: Old versions keep old vulnerabilities; a version without a funeral never dies.
checks.validate: Deprecated versions have retirement dates, sunset headers, deprecation notices, and eventually die.

variants.name: Version census
variants.payload: Enumerate every responding version (paths, headers, content negotiation); check Sunset/Deprecation headers.
variants.expect: Every non-current version scheduled with communicated dates; unmaintained elders listed for the report.
variants.why: The census itself is the finding generator.

variants.name: Policy parity probe
variants.payload: Re-run two strong authorization checks against the oldest version.
variants.expect: Parity enforced; weaker behavior on elders reported with evidence.
variants.why: Security debt concentrates in versions.

variants.name: Sunset honesty
variants.payload: Where Sunset headers exist, verify the date matches the communicated plan.
variants.expect: Consistent, honest headers — clients get a fair warning.
variants.why: Sunset dates are commitments; verify they are kept.

checks.title: Shadow and environment APIs discovered safely
checks.why: Shadow deployments (test APIs on prod domains, one-off endpoints) carry prod data without prod controls.
checks.validate: Shadow and environment-specific deployments are identified, scoped, and either brought under policy or isolated.

variants.name: Subdomain census
variants.payload: In-scope DNS/certificate transparency for api-ish subdomains (api-test., staging., dev., internal.); probe harmlessly.
variants.expect: Findings mapped and owner-assigned; prod-data-on-test-config reported.
variants.why: CT logs are the free API census.

variants.name: Bundle route extraction
variants.payload: Extract routes/endpoints from shipped JS bundles; diff against the owned inventory.
variants.expect: Unaccounted routes become inventory entries or findings.
variants.why: The client knows all the doors.

variants.name: Cross-environment bleed
variants.payload: Compare auth acceptance: does the staging API accept production tokens (or vice versa) within authorized scope?
variants.expect: Environment tokens are environment-bound.
variants.why: Bleed turns test APIs into prod backdoors.

checks.title: Documentation reconciled with deployed operations
checks.why: Drift between OpenAPI and reality hides both missing functions and ghost endpoints from review.
checks.validate: Documentation matches deployed operations within stated tolerance; drift is visible and owned.

variants.name: Schema diff
variants.payload: Fetch the live OpenAPI/GraphQL schema; diff paths, methods, params, and response shapes against documented behavior.
variants.expect: Drift list produced and reviewed with the owner; unexplained drift becomes findings.
variants.why: The diff is cheap; the conversation is the value.

variants.name: Ghost endpoints
variants.payload: Call documented-but-absent endpoints (removed features).
variants.expect: Clean 404/410 with documented retirement — not half-alive handlers.
variants.why: Dead docs describe live risks.

variants.name: Tolerance policy
variants.payload: Where documented drift tolerance exists, verify observed drift is inside it.
variants.expect: Drift within policy or policy updated.
variants.why: Tolerated drift is still drift.

checks.title: Third-party API data validated and authorized
checks.why: Data from partners and webhooks is attacker-influenced — trusting it is an unauthenticated input path.
checks.validate: Inbound third-party data is signature-verified, schema-validated, and permission-checked before use.

variants.name: Webhook signature
variants.payload: Inspect webhook verification (HMAC/signature headers); replay a captured webhook of your own event with tampered payload.
variants.expect: Tampered payload rejected; replay within timestamp window only.
variants.why: Unsigned webhooks are unauthenticated APIs.

variants.name: Payload validation
variants.payload: Submit webhook/provider callbacks with oversized, mistyped, and injection-bearing fields (harmless canaries).
variants.expect: Schema-validated; junk rejected before processing or storage.
variants.why: Partner fields get the same validation as user fields.

variants.name: Authority from context
variants.payload: Check whether actions triggered by callbacks run with caller or service authority for foreign objects.
variants.expect: Callback authority is scoped; third-party input cannot steer privileged actions (see confused-deputy).
variants.why: Inbound trust is authority you granted.

checks.title: Consumed APIs: timeouts, sizes, and failure handling
checks.why: A hung third-party call hangs your users; unbounded responses and unclear failures cascade into outages.
checks.validate: Upstream calls carry timeouts, size caps, and defined failure modes (fail-closed where security-relevant).

variants.name: Slow-endpoint shape
variants.payload: Point a fetch-preview/import at an endpoint you control that drip-feeds bytes slowly (within authorized testing).
variants.expect: Client-side timeout engages; request abandoned with a clean error.
variants.why: Your own slow server proves their timeout exists.

variants.name: Huge-response bound
variants.payload: Serve a large payload from your controlled endpoint to a fetch/import feature.
variants.expect: Response size capped before parsing; memory-safe failure.
variants.why: Caps belong before parsers.

variants.name: Failure-mode review
variants.payload: Ask/observe behavior when the upstream is down or erroring (sandbox, owner-assisted).
variants.expect: Defined degradation — fail-closed for security decisions, graceful for UX.
variants.why: Failure is a design state, not an accident.

checks.title: Upstream TLS identity and redirect policy
checks.why: Server-to-server calls with disabled verification or permissive redirects are MITM invitations with service authority.
checks.validate: Upstream TLS verifies certificates (CA + hostname); redirect hops revalidate; no verification bypass flags.

variants.name: Certificate mismatch probe
variants.payload: Where you can observe upstream config (review or owner question), confirm verification is on; attempt a self-signed upstream only in owner-approved test hooks.
variants.expect: Verification failures abort the call — never a warning-tolerated fetch.
variants.why: Verification-off is the quiet classic.

variants.name: Redirect-policy probe
variants.payload: Upstream URL (test hook or review) that redirects cross-host.
variants.expect: Cross-host redirects refused or revalidated — authority does not follow redirects blindly.
variants.why: Redirects change destination; policy must re-decide.

variants.name: Scheme downgrade
variants.payload: An http:// upstream target (or redirect) for a documented-https integration.
variants.expect: Plaintext upstreams refused; integrations pinned to https.
variants.why: Downgrade removes every guarantee.

checks.title: Upstream credentials least-privileged and server-side
checks.why: The backend credential vault is the deputy full of keys — one broad key turns every confused-deputy into a breach.
checks.validate: Upstream credentials are scoped to minimum needs, stored server-side, rotated, and never logged.

variants.name: Scope review
variants.payload: With the owner, review each integration credential's actual granted scope vs its used scope.
variants.expect: Granted ~= used; excess scopes removed (evidence for the report).
variants.why: Least privilege is a diff, not a feeling.

variants.name: Credential-in-log sweep
variants.payload: Inspect application logs (owner-assisted) and error payloads for upstream keys, bearer tokens, and secrets.
variants.expect: No credentials in logs, errors, or client responses.
variants.why: Logs outlive the requests that made them.

variants.name: Rotation reality
variants.payload: Ask/observe the rotation procedure; verify old credentials fail after rotation in a test window.
variants.expect: Rotation works end-to-end; old keys dead — not just replaced.
variants.why: Rotation without revocation is accumulation.

bola-path.purpose: Reading another tenant's object via its path id with your token is the canonical BOLA.
bola-path.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>

csrf-simple-json.purpose: A text/plain JSON POST skips a preflight and can be CSRF'd unless a token is required.
csrf-simple-json.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example

{"status":"cancelled"}

collaborator-url.purpose: A controlled HTTPS callback confirms the server makes the outbound request.
collaborator-url.payload:
POST /api/v1/hooks HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"url":"https://unique.oast.example/wapt"}
